'''''Herugavialis''''' ("[[Horus]] gharial") is an [[extinct]] genus of marine [[gavialoid]] crocodilian known from the [[Eocene]] ([[Lutetian|Lutetian stage]]) [[Mokattam Formation]] of Egypt.<ref name="Herugavialis" /> It contains a [[monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Herugavialis cairensis''''', known from near [[Cairo]], Egypt.<ref name="b" /><ref name="c" /> ''Herugavialis'' did not have a [[maxilla]] process within its [[lacrimal gland]], whereas all [[extant taxon|extant]] (living) [[crocodilian]]s do.<ref name="d" /> 

The species was originally described in the genus ''[[Tomistoma]]'', which contains a single living species, the [[false gharial]], and remained there for nearly a century, even after more comprehensive studies found it to not belong to the genus. In a 2026 study, it was moved to its own genus, ''Herugavialis''. This genus name references the Ancient Egyptian god Horus, widely thought to be depicted in the [[Great Sphinx of Giza|Great Sphinx]] (built from the same geological formation that ''Herugavialis'' was identified from), as well as the Sphinx's lack of a nose, referencing the missing nasal region ([[premaxilla]]) of the [[holotype]] skull of ''Herugavialis''.<ref name="Herugavialis" />

== Classification ==
[[File:Herugavialis cairensis (holotype, SMNS 10575 - dorsal and ventral).png|thumb|upright|Holotype skull in dorsal (top) and ventral (bottom) views]]
In a 2018, Lee & Yates conducted a phylogenetic anlaysis simultaneously using [[morphology (biology)|morphological]], molecular ([[DNA sequencing]]), and [[stratigraphic]] ([[fossil]] age) data. They recovered ''Tomistoma cairense'' as a [[gavialoid]], more [[basal (phylogeny)|basal]] than the [[last common ancestor]] of both the [[gharial]] (''Gavialis gangeticus'') and the [[false gharial]] (''Tomistoma schlegelii''):<ref name="LeeYates2018"/>

[[File:Herugavialis cairensis (paleoart by Karim Zanaty).png|thumb|''Herugavialis'' portrait and skull anachronistically depicted alongside the [[The Great Sphinx]] and [[pyramids of Giza]]]]
''Tomistoma cairense'' was placed in the new genus ''Herugavialis'' in 2026, acknowledging that its inclusion within ''Tomistoma'' rendered that genus [[paraphyletic]]. ''Herugavialis'' was recovered more closely related to the gharial than the false gharial, within Gavialidae.
